newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asian traders braced for further LME copper falls.
newsitem.headline: Asian traders braced for further LME copper falls.

text.p: Copper prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) are set to fall nearer to $2,250 after breaching a key support point at $2,300 late on Tuesday, Asian traders said on Wednesday.
Three-month copper "has fallen through its major support at $2,355, set during the recent upward trend which started in November", said a trader at a leading Japanese trading house.
"Though we might see a small recovery, it is likely to slip further towards $2,250 and then $2,200," he said.

Traders said copper, which shrugged off news of a strike at Portugal's Neves Corvo copper mine, could be hit further by a shift by U.S. funds towards better-performing U.S. stocks from base metals and precious metals.
At 0450 GMT, three-month copper was quoted at $2,287/$2,297 per tonne, down slightly from $2,290/$2,294 at 1800 GMT on Tuesday and the kerb close at $2,368.
Asian traders were also worried that some 10,000 tonnes of South Korean copper and another 20,000 tonnes of Chinese copper were to arrive in Singapore in the near future.
Traders said the fall in copper was unlikely to leave other metals untouched, even those with strong fundamentals or bullish factors, such as aluminium and nickel.

"The support (for aluminium) at $1,550 is pretty strong, but it can't completely ignore copper's movements," said one trader. "Should it breach the support, we might see quite heavy stop-loss selling."
Another trader said: "Nickel will try the next support at $6,750 today or tomorrow.

"Though we heard the news about a possible strike at Falconbridge (Ltd in Canada), you have to remember, in the end, the price didn't move much on the news of the strike at the Inco (Ltd) plant," the trader said.
At 0300 GMT, aluminium was at $1,561/$1,566, up from $1,555/$1,557 at 1800 GMT and the kerb close at $1,565 on Tuesday.
Traders said zinc, on the other hand, remained on an upward trend despite a possible pause following a sharp advance over the last few weeks.
"It might drop to as low as $1,420, but there will be no change in the upward trend. They also say China has quite a large short position around September," one trader said.

On Tuesday, industry sources in China said Chinese state metals units and Swiss trading house Glencore were still trying to resolve a dispute over the quality of Chinese zinc that could threaten the long-standing links between them. -- Tokyo Commodities +81-3-3432-6179
